crib.title: Crib slats too far apart
crib.q: Are the slats no more than 2-3/8 inches apart?
crib.fix: Measure the gaps between slats. If any gap is wider than 2-3/8 inches, stop using this crib and replace it.

source.title: Suitable Sleeping Sites: Safe at Night & Naptime

crib.title: Crib has a drop side
crib.q: Does the crib have four sides that do not move (no drop side)?
crib.fix: Full-sized cribs should have four immovable sides. Replace a crib that has a drop side.

source.title: Suitable Sleeping Sites: Safe at Night & Naptime

crib.title: Mattress does not fit snugly
crib.q: Does the mattress fit snugly, with no gaps that could trap an arm, leg or head?
crib.fix: Replace the mattress with one made for this crib so no gap is left at the sides.

source.title: Suitable Sleeping Sites: Safe at Night & Naptime

crib.title: Extras in the crib
crib.q: Is the crib free of bumpers, pillows and stuffed toys, with only a snugly fitted sheet in it?
crib.fix: Take bumpers, pillows and stuffed animals out. Leave only a snugly fitted sheet in the first year.

source.title: Suitable Sleeping Sites: Safe at Night & Naptime

crib.title: Loose crib sheet
crib.q: Is the fitted sheet snug enough that it will not slip off?
crib.fix: Switch to a fitted sheet made for this mattress size so it stays tight on all corners.

source.title: Suitable Sleeping Sites: Safe at Night & Naptime

crib.title: Mobile within reach
crib.q: Is any mobile hung out of reach, and taken down once the baby can sit up?
crib.fix: Move the mobile higher or take it down. Mobiles should come down once the baby can sit up.

source.title: Suitable Sleeping Sites: Safe at Night & Naptime

crib.title: Crib placed near hazards
crib.q: Is the crib away from windows and at least an arm's length from dressers or tabletops?
crib.fix: Move the crib away from windows and at least an arm's length from dressers and tabletops. Take down picture frames and mirrors above it.

source.title: Suitable Sleeping Sites: Safe at Night & Naptime

crib.title: Mattress height not lowered
crib.q: Have you lowered the mattress as your baby has grown?
crib.fix: Lower the mattress. It should be at its lowest setting by the time your baby can sit or stand.

source.title: Suitable Sleeping Sites: Safe at Night & Naptime

bassinet.title: Bassinet limits not followed
bassinet.q: Is your baby within the maker's weight and age limits for this bassinet?
bassinet.fix: Check the label and manual for the limits. Move your baby to a crib once they reach them.

source.title: Cribs, Bassinets, & Pack and Plays

bassinet.title: Baby is outgrowing the bassinet
bassinet.q: Is your baby younger than about 5 months and not yet pushing up on hands and knees?
bassinet.fix: Stop using the bassinet by about 5 months, or once your baby can push up on hands and knees. Move to a crib.

source.title: CPSC Approves New Federal Safety Standard for Bassinets and Cradles

bassinet.title: Wrong mattress in bassinet
bassinet.q: Is the mattress the one that came with the bassinet (or a replacement from the maker)?
bassinet.fix: Use only the mattress that came with the bassinet. Order a replacement from the manufacturer if it is lost or worn.

source.title: Cribs, Bassinets, & Pack and Plays

bassinet.title: Extra padding in bassinet
bassinet.q: Is the bassinet free of added pillows, cushions or mattress toppers?
bassinet.fix: Remove pillows, cushions and toppers from under and on top of the mattress. Memory foam toppers are not recommended for babies.

source.title: Cribs, Bassinets, & Pack and Plays

bassinet.title: Bassinet may predate the federal standard
bassinet.q: Was the bassinet made in 2013 or later, after the federal standard for bassinets and cradles began?
bassinet.fix: Look for the manufacture date on the label. If it is older than 2013 or you cannot find it, consider replacing it.

source.title: Cribs, Bassinets, & Pack and Plays

bassinet.title: Bassinet recall not checked
bassinet.q: Have you run a recall check on this bassinet?
bassinet.fix: Use the Check recalls button on this item, and do not use a recalled bassinet.

source.title: CPSC Approves New Federal Safety Standard for Bassinets and Cradles

car_seat.title: Child may be forward-facing too early
car_seat.q: Does your child ride rear-facing (children under age 1 should always ride rear-facing, and rear-facing is best for as long as the seat allows)?
car_seat.fix: Turn the seat to face the rear. NHTSA recommends keeping children rear-facing as long as possible.

source.title: Car Seat & Booster Seat Safety, Ratings, Guidelines

car_seat.title: Car seat installed with both anchors and belt
car_seat.q: Is the seat installed with either the lower anchors or the seat belt, never both?
car_seat.fix: Reinstall using the lower anchors or the vehicle seat belt, not both. Read the weight limit for the lower anchors on the seat's label.

source.title: Car Seat & Booster Seat Safety, Ratings, Guidelines

car_seat.title: Tether not used
car_seat.q: If the seat faces forward, is the top tether attached?
car_seat.fix: Attach and tighten the top tether. NHTSA recommends always using a tether with a forward-facing seat.

source.title: Car Seat & Booster Seat Safety, Ratings, Guidelines

car_seat.title: Harness straps at the wrong height
car_seat.q: Are the harness straps at or below the shoulders (rear-facing) or at or above the shoulders (forward-facing)?
car_seat.fix: Move the straps to the correct slot for the way the seat faces.

source.title: How To Use a Car Seat Harness
source.publisher: NHTSA (copy hosted by Brown University Health)

car_seat.title: Chest clip in the wrong place
car_seat.q: Is the chest clip at armpit level?
car_seat.fix: Slide the chest clip up to armpit level.

source.title: How To Use a Car Seat Harness
source.publisher: NHTSA (copy hosted by Brown University Health)

car_seat.title: Harness too loose
car_seat.q: Does the harness pass the pinch test (you cannot pinch webbing at the shoulder)?
car_seat.fix: Tighten the harness until your fingers slide off the webbing at the shoulder and you cannot pinch any.

source.title: How To Use a Car Seat Harness
source.publisher: NHTSA (copy hosted by Brown University Health)

car_seat.title: Car seat not registered
car_seat.q: Is the seat registered with the manufacturer?
car_seat.fix: Register the seat with the manufacturer to get recall and safety notices. The NHTSA SaferCar app or email alerts also work.

source.title: Car Seat & Booster Seat Safety, Ratings, Guidelines

car_seat.title: Used or crashed seat not checked
car_seat.q: If the seat is second-hand or was in a crash, have you used NHTSA's used-seat checklist and crash guidance?
car_seat.fix: Read NHTSA's used car seat checklist and its guidance on seats after a crash before using this seat.

source.title: Car Seat & Booster Seat Safety, Ratings, Guidelines

booster.title: Booster used too early
booster.q: Has your child outgrown the forward-facing harness seat?
booster.fix: A child who still fits the harness seat should stay in it. Move to a booster once the harness limits are outgrown.

source.title: Car Seat & Booster Seat Safety, Ratings, Guidelines

booster.title: Booster in the front seat
booster.q: Does your child ride in the back seat?
booster.fix: Move the booster and your child to the back seat.

source.title: Car Seat & Booster Seat Safety, Ratings, Guidelines

booster.title: Lap belt across the stomach
booster.q: Does the lap belt lie across the upper thighs, not the stomach?
booster.fix: Re-route the belt so the lap belt lies low across the upper thighs.

source.title: Car Seat & Booster Seat Safety, Ratings, Guidelines

booster.title: Booster not registered
booster.q: Is the booster registered with the manufacturer?
booster.fix: Register the seat with the manufacturer to receive recall notices.

source.title: Car Seat & Booster Seat Safety, Ratings, Guidelines

booster.title: Used or crashed booster not checked
booster.q: If the booster is second-hand or was in a crash, have you used NHTSA's used-seat checklist and crash guidance?
booster.fix: Read NHTSA's used car seat checklist and its guidance on seats after a crash before using this booster.

source.title: Car Seat & Booster Seat Safety, Ratings, Guidelines

high_chair.title: High chair straps not used
high_chair.q: Do you use the straps every time, including the crotch strap?
high_chair.fix: Buckle every strap, including the crotch strap, each time your child sits in the chair.

source.title: 6 Quick High Chair Safety Tips

high_chair.title: Child stands in high chair
high_chair.q: Does your child stay seated, never standing in the chair?
high_chair.fix: Do not let your child stand in the high chair. Lift them out when they want to move.

source.title: 6 Quick High Chair Safety Tips

high_chair.title: High chair tips easily
high_chair.q: Is the chair stable, so it cannot be tipped over easily?
high_chair.fix: Test the chair by pushing on it. If it tips easily, stop using it and choose a more stable one.

source.title: 6 Quick High Chair Safety Tips

high_chair.title: Folding locks not engaged
high_chair.q: If the chair folds, are the locks engaged every time you set it up?
high_chair.fix: Check that the folding locks click into place each time you open the chair.

source.title: 6 Quick High Chair Safety Tips

high_chair.title: High chair next to counter or table
high_chair.q: Is the chair kept away from counters and tables that a child could push against?
high_chair.fix: Move the chair away from counters and tables so your child cannot push off and tip it.

source.title: 6 Quick High Chair Safety Tips

high_chair.title: Clip-on chair not secure
high_chair.q: If you use a clip-on chair, does it lock onto a table that can hold your child's weight without tipping?
high_chair.fix: Use a model that locks onto the table, and make sure the table is steady and your child's feet cannot reach a table support.

source.title: 6 Quick High Chair Safety Tips

high_chair.title: Child left alone in high chair
high_chair.q: Is your child always watched while in the chair?
high_chair.fix: Stay with your young child while they are in the high chair, and keep older children from climbing on it.

source.title: 6 Quick High Chair Safety Tips

stroller.title: Stroller brakes
stroller.q: Do the brakes work easily, and do you set them whenever the stroller is stopped?
stroller.fix: Set the brakes every time you stop. Make sure your child cannot reach the release.

source.title: How to Choose a Safe Baby Stroller

stroller.title: Stroller harness not used
stroller.q: Do you use a five-point harness on every ride?
stroller.fix: Buckle the harness on every ride. For infants, rolled blankets on each side can limit slouching.

source.title: How to Choose a Safe Baby Stroller

stroller.title: Bags hung on handles
stroller.q: Is the stroller free of bags hanging from the handles?
stroller.fix: Take bags off the handles. If there is a basket, keep heavy items low and near the rear wheels.

source.title: How to Choose a Safe Baby Stroller

stroller.title: Frame not locked open
stroller.q: Do you lock the frame open before you put your child in, keeping them clear while folding?
stroller.fix: Lock the frame open before seating your child, and keep your child away while folding or unfolding.

source.title: How to Choose a Safe Baby Stroller

stroller.title: Toys strung across stroller
stroller.q: Are toys strung across the stroller secured, and removed once the baby can sit up?
stroller.fix: Secure the toys, and remove them once your baby can sit up or rise onto hands and knees.

source.title: How to Choose a Safe Baby Stroller

stroller.title: Child left alone in stroller
stroller.q: Is your child never left alone in the stroller, and kept in sight if they fall asleep?
stroller.fix: Keep your child in sight whenever they are in the stroller, including while asleep.

source.title: How to Choose a Safe Baby Stroller

play_yard.title: Torn or large-holed mesh
play_yard.q: Is the mesh intact, with holes no larger than 1/4 inch?
play_yard.fix: Check the mesh for tears and for holes larger than 1/4 inch. Stop using a play yard with damaged mesh.

source.title: Choosing Safe Baby Products: Playpens
source.publisher: Nemours KidsHealth (copy hosted by Rady Children's Hospital)

play_yard.title: Hinges and rails
play_yard.q: Are the hinges well protected, and do the top rails lock when raised?
play_yard.fix: Raise the rails until they lock. Stop using the play yard if the hinges or supports are damaged.

source.title: Choosing Safe Baby Products: Playpens
source.publisher: Nemours KidsHealth (copy hosted by Rady Children's Hospital)

play_yard.title: Play yard sides too low
play_yard.q: Are the sides at least 20 inches high, measured from the floor of the play yard?
play_yard.fix: Measure from the floor of the play yard. If the sides are lower than 20 inches, choose a different play yard.

source.title: Choosing Safe Baby Products: Playpens
source.publisher: Nemours KidsHealth (copy hosted by Rady Children's Hospital)

play_yard.title: Wrong or stacked mattress pad
play_yard.q: Is there only one firm pad (about 1 inch thick), made for this play yard?
play_yard.fix: Use only the pad that came with the play yard, or a replacement from the maker. Never add a second pad or swap in one that may not fit.

source.title: Choosing Safe Baby Products: Playpens
source.publisher: Nemours KidsHealth (copy hosted by Rady Children's Hospital)

play_yard.title: Extra padding in play yard
play_yard.q: Is the play yard free of extra pillows, cushions or toppers?
play_yard.fix: Remove added padding. Use only the mattress made for this play yard.

source.title: Cribs, Bassinets, & Pack and Plays

play_yard.title: Mesh side left lowered
play_yard.q: Are the side-lowering locks out of your baby's reach, and the side never left down with your baby inside?
play_yard.fix: Raise and lock the side before you step away. Keep the locks out of your baby's reach.

source.title: Choosing Safe Baby Products: Playpens
source.publisher: Nemours KidsHealth (copy hosted by Rady Children's Hospital)

play_yard.title: Used play yard worn or diamond openings
play_yard.q: If it is used, is the floor free of wear and tear, and are there no large diamond-shaped openings?
play_yard.fix: Check the floor for wear and tear and avoid play yards with large diamond-shaped openings.

source.title: Choosing Safe Baby Products: Playpens
source.publisher: Nemours KidsHealth (copy hosted by Rady Children's Hospital)

bouncer_swing.title: Swing straps not buckled
bouncer_swing.q: Do you always buckle the straps, including shoulder straps when your baby sits up?
bouncer_swing.fix: Buckle the straps every time your baby is in the seat.

source.title: Can Babies Sleep in a Swing? Safety Risks Explained
source.publisher: Sleep Foundation (reports AAP and CPSC guidance)

bouncer_swing.title: Swing or bouncer on a raised surface
bouncer_swing.q: Is the seat always on the floor, never on a crib, mattress or other raised surface?
bouncer_swing.fix: Place the seat on the floor. The AAP advises against putting it on a crib, mattress or other raised surface.

source.title: Can Babies Sleep in a Swing? Safety Risks Explained
source.publisher: Sleep Foundation (reports AAP and CPSC guidance)

bouncer_swing.title: Swing angle for a young baby
bouncer_swing.q: If your baby is under 4 months, is the swing tilted to its flattest position?
bouncer_swing.fix: Tilt the swing to its flattest position for babies under 4 months.

source.title: Can Babies Sleep in a Swing? Safety Risks Explained
source.publisher: Sleep Foundation (reports AAP and CPSC guidance)

bouncer_swing.title: Baby sleeping in the seat
bouncer_swing.q: If your baby falls asleep in it, do you move them to a crib or bassinet?
bouncer_swing.fix: Move a sleeping baby to a crib or bassinet with a firm surface and nothing soft in it.

source.title: Can Babies Sleep in a Swing? Safety Risks Explained
source.publisher: Sleep Foundation (reports AAP and CPSC guidance)

bouncer_swing.title: Long stretches in the seat
bouncer_swing.q: Do you limit the time your baby spends in the swing or bouncer, and watch them while they are in it?
bouncer_swing.fix: Keep sessions short and stay close. The AAP says babies should not spend a long time in swings or similar equipment.

source.title: Can Babies Sleep in a Swing? Safety Risks Explained
source.publisher: Sleep Foundation (reports AAP and CPSC guidance)

bouncer_swing.title: Swing or bouncer recall not checked
bouncer_swing.q: Have you run a recall check on this swing or bouncer?
bouncer_swing.fix: Use the Check recalls button on this item, and stop using it if it matches a recall.

source.title: Can Babies Sleep in a Swing? Safety Risks Explained
source.publisher: Sleep Foundation (reports AAP and CPSC guidance)

baby_gate.title: Pressure gate at top of stairs
baby_gate.q: If the gate is at the top of stairs, is it hardware-mounted to the door frame?
baby_gate.fix: Use a hardware-mounted gate at the top of stairs. Pressure-mounted gates are for doorways and the bottom of stairs.

source.title: Choosing Safe Baby Products: Gates

baby_gate.title: Swing-out gate at top of stairs
baby_gate.q: Is the gate free of a swing-out design at the top of stairs?
baby_gate.fix: Swing-out gates should never go at the top of stairs. Replace it with a hardware-mounted gate that does not swing out.

source.title: Choosing Safe Baby Products: Gates

baby_gate.title: No safety certification label
baby_gate.q: Does the gate carry an ASTM/JPMA certification label?
baby_gate.fix: Look for the ASTM/JPMA certification on the label. If it is missing, choose a certified gate.

source.title: Choosing Safe Baby Products: Gates

baby_gate.title: Old accordion gate
baby_gate.q: Is the gate free of diamond-shaped openings with wide Vs at the top (old accordion style)?
baby_gate.fix: Replace old accordion gates. The V-shaped openings can trap a baby's head.

source.title: Choosing Safe Baby Products: Gates

baby_gate.title: Gate bars too far apart
baby_gate.q: Are the vertical bars or slats no more than 2-3/8 inches apart?
baby_gate.fix: Measure the gaps between bars. If any gap is wider than 2-3/8 inches, replace the gate.

source.title: Choosing Safe Baby Products: Gates

baby_gate.title: Gap under the gate
baby_gate.q: Is the space under the gate no more than 1 to 2 inches?
baby_gate.fix: Measure the gap at the floor. Adjust or replace the gate if it is larger than 1 to 2 inches.

source.title: Choosing Safe Baby Products: Gates

baby_gate.title: Gate too short
baby_gate.q: Is the gate at least three-quarters of your child's height?
baby_gate.fix: Measure your child. Replace the gate if it is shorter than three-quarters of their height.

source.title: Choosing Safe Baby Products: Gates

baby_gate.title: Child can open or climb the gate
baby_gate.q: Can your child not open or climb the gate?
baby_gate.fix: If your child can open or climb the gate, take it down. Keep large toys away from the gate.

source.title: Choosing Safe Baby Products: Gates

changing_table.title: Changing table guardrail
changing_table.q: Does the table have a 2-inch guardrail on all four sides?
changing_table.fix: Replace the table or pad with one that has a 2-inch guardrail on all four sides.

source.title: Changing Table Safety

changing_table.title: Flat changing surface
changing_table.q: Is the changing surface concave, with the centre slightly lower than the edges?
changing_table.fix: Use a contoured changing pad with the centre lower than the edges.

source.title: Changing Table Safety

changing_table.title: Changing table strap not used
changing_table.q: Do you buckle the safety strap each time?
changing_table.fix: Buckle the strap each time. Do not rely on it alone.

source.title: Changing Table Safety

changing_table.title: Hand off the baby
changing_table.q: Do you keep one hand on your baby at all times, even briefly?
changing_table.fix: Keep one hand on your baby the whole time, even when the strap is buckled.

source.title: Changing Table Safety

changing_table.title: Supplies out of reach
changing_table.q: Are diapering supplies within your reach but out of your baby's reach?
changing_table.fix: Rearrange supplies so you can reach them without letting go, and your baby cannot.

source.title: Changing Table Safety

changing_table.title: Powder within reach
changing_table.q: Are powder containers kept away from your baby?
changing_table.fix: Store powder away from your baby. Inhaled powder can injure the lungs.

source.title: Changing Table Safety

changing_table.title: Diapers stored within reach
changing_table.q: Are disposable diapers stored out of reach, with worn diapers covered by clothing?
changing_table.fix: Store diapers out of reach, and cover a worn diaper with clothing so the plastic liner is not exposed.

source.title: Changing Table Safety
